reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and holiday detection, but repeats the daily skip-versus-move policy instead of extending one shared definition.

duplication.why: The daily-frequency policy is repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and createScheduleList.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but server handlers and budget code also independently decide schedule adjustment policy.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling changes, their data plumbing, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several implementations of the same policy, separate occurrence-search heuristics, and an untyped config parameter despite an existing RecurConfig type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange implement daily skipping outside applyWeekendRule, while createScheduleList independently selects when to bypass adjustment through getNextDate's noSkipWeekend argument.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily skip-versus-move decision appears as a find predicate in getNextDate, a filter in getUpcomingDates, a loop branch in getDatesInRange, and the inverse movesWeekends flag in createScheduleList.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and createScheduleList independently dispatch daily skipping versus moving.
